confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for Split prices. The food and drink figures come mainly from 2026 travel and cost guides, which give estimates rather than posted menu prices. They disagree with each other, and I could not retrieve Numbeo or Expatistan item-level Split pages. Drink and meal anchors use typical mid-city prices with a modest lift for July peak season and Riva-waterfront premiums. Euro prices were converted to USD at an assumed EUR/USD of about 1.16, which I did not search for. Cocktail and wine come from guide ranges (cocktail about €10-15, house wine about €4-7), not from a ratio to beer. The midrange two-person meal is the weakest food anchor: it combines a Croatia-wide three-course figure of about €30 per person with a July peak uplift. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season. They are not based on live listings or booking pages, so they carry the most uncertainty.
comparable_city_reasoning: Split is a high-season Adriatic coastal tourist city. It is cheaper than Dubrovnik and Hvar, roughly in line with Italian and Spanish coastal cities such as Naples and Malaga, and cheaper than Western European capitals. Pricing leans on Croatian coastal-city guides and Expatistan city comparisons.
